name: AI-enabled drug discovery
summary: AI proposes targets, molecules and experiments that researchers test in laboratories and clinical trials.
useCase: A discovery team prioritises compounds predicted to meet several constraints, then measures whether they actually work in biological experiments.
whyNow: AI-designed programmes have reached clinical trials and one randomized phase 2a study has been published for an AI-discovered target and molecule. Pipeline activity is growing faster than the evidence for improved end-to-end drug success.

mainstream.scope: AI integrated into routine discovery and optimisation workflows at pharmaceutical companies; not a promise that AI-origin drugs all reach approval.
mainstream.rationale: Software and experimental integration already have commercial buyers. Routine workflow adoption should precede a definitive industry-wide improvement in clinical success, which takes years to measure. Clinical attrition remains the main economic uncertainty.

metric.name: Insilico cumulative nominated preclinical candidates
metric.scope: One AI-drug-discovery company, reported candidate nominations
metric.limitations: Company-reported preclinical nominations are an activity proxy, not approvals, successful medicines or an industry total. The 2026 value is a cumulative April observation. Candidate quality and trial outcomes matter more than counts.
metric.futureNote: No defensible like-for-like external forecast is available for this KPI. The forward maturity path is a separately labelled analyst scenario, not a numerical adoption forecast.

milestones.text: The company dates its series of preclinical candidate nominations from 2021.
Insilico announced a phase 1 programme for its AI-discovered fibrosis candidate.
No comparable annual candidate count is included for 2023.
Insilico reported 20 nominated preclinical candidates by November.
A randomized phase 2a report for rentosertib was published; Insilico later listed publicly in Hong Kong.
An April company release described its thirtieth preclinical candidate. This is pipeline output, not an approved-drug count.

tailwinds: Better biological data and experimentally grounded models
Pharma partnerships fund work before product approval
Robotics and assays can turn model suggestions into measured feedback
bottlenecks: Training data can be biased or poorly matched to patients
A molecule can be easy to design but hard to make, deliver or prove
Long trials delay proof that discovery efficiency improves final returns
watchMetrics: Prospective hit rates and time to validated candidate
Clinical progression and failures against comparable non-AI programmes
Cash revenue and research economics versus headline partnership milestones
